children: Thailand's consumer prices likely rose 2.31% on year in August, according to the median estimate of five economists polled by The Wall Street Journal. That would be sharper than July's 1.95% increase. Prices likely rose mainly due to higher domestic fuel prices last month, which could have pushed up transportation inflation, ANZ Research's Kausani Basak says in a report. However, inflationary pressures remain manageable and within the Bank of Thailand's 1%-3% target range, she adds. Given weaker growth momentum in 2Q, ANZ expects the BOT to hold its policy rate steady at 1.00% in October. Inflation data are due next week. (amanda.lee@wsj.com)
